#36822. What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 13m • 📚 Deep Dive (2585 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Cbssports ↗ Open Full Page

What needs to happen for Manchester United to get relegated from the Premier League?

📅 11 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 13 min read (2585 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~13 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • The answer to that is probably not but the fact that, after Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Manchester United being relegated to the Championship is a prospect that can be discussed as anything other than rival fan fiction ought to terrify the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.
  • Recent findings suggest that A quarter of the season is gone.
  • That is why Michael Carrick had to go.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It couldn't happen, could it? The answer to that is probably not but the fact that, after Sunday's 4-4 draw with Aston Villa, Manchester United being relegated to the Championship is a prospect that can be discussed as anything other than rival fan fiction ought to terrify the Glazers and Sir Jim Ratcliffe.

Recent findings suggest that A quarter of the season is gone. The table may not be telling us the whole story but it can no longer be dismissed like it can in August or September. You'll struggle to find many teams who can sincerely argue they've been mistreated by the fixture list and United are certainly not one of them. They are where they are, 18th, a point behind Coventry City and safety, and there is not much to explain that away.

That is why Michael Carrick had to go. On Wednesday morning, the 45-year-old was still taking training at the club's Carrington base but he is expected to be relieved of his duties once the United hierarchy have met in Monaco. There, the club's chief executive Omar Berrada and director of football Jason Wilcox are expected to tell minority owner Sir Jim Ratcliffe that it is time to part ways with Carrick. Meanwhile, talks have already begun for USMNT head coach Mauricio Pochettino to take the helm, returning to the Premier League two and a half years after leaving Chelsea and mere months after signing a newly introduced deal with US Soccer. It would appear that unfinished business in England -- and the Old Trafford vacancy to which he has been linked for so long -- has tempted the Argentine away on the eve of the CONCACAF Nations League quarterfinals.

The path Pochettino is now on is one fraught with risk. And yet coaching for survival and nothing else would be the latest in a line of clumsy decisions from the Old Trafford hierarchy. Projection models such as Opta's would probably make the case that this team is dicing with danger but, with a 22% chance of relegation, will probably be fine. Bookmakers too are pretty skeptical that United's 2027-28 will encompass trips to Blackburn and Millwall with eight or so teams priced as more likely to go down than the Red Devils. That will be informed by an analytics profile that really does not suggest United are one of the three worst teams in the Premier League.

Through 10 games, a sample size where expected goals (xG) is more predictive than goals and scorelines when it comes to future results, United have an xG difference of -0.27. If there is an average team in the division, it's Carrick's. Naturally, that is not good enough for a team with their aspirations. Another 28 games putting up those underlying numbers and United will live to fight another day.

Industry observers note that suppose they don't. As anyone that saw Sunday's game can attest, events with a significantly less than 22% probability can happen all the time. A team's xG profile doesn't always capture everything. If it did, Villa would have notably fewer than their 13 points. Things could go worse for United. Let's have a look at how that might happen.

It has been revealed that carrick departs Old Trafford with his reputation among the fanbase still intact. He might also find that future employers look more forgivingly on his time at United. His tally of 47 points from 27 league games was bettered only by Manchester City and Arsenal, a goal difference of plus-10 putting United behind those two, Bournemouth and Brighton.

In a recent development, equally, momentum had turned. With a full pre-season to establish his ideas (rather than hone Ruben Amorim's), Carrick seems to have crafted a team who are less effective in attack and more porous in defense. The 4-4-2/4-2-4 in which his team line up out of position has been easily manipulated by superior teams and structural complications are not offset by intensity off the ball. United rank 15th for pressures applied and 10th for passes per defensive action, both measures of pressing applied by a team. Meanwhile, the attack has both been creating fewer chances -- the comeback against Villa notwithstanding -- and being more wasteful with them. It is a bad cocktail.

The risk would have been that United reaffirmed the commitment they made to Carrick after the three-goal defeats to Como and Bournemouth, one which always seemed to be conditioned on the imminent international break. Could anyone parachuted in at a moment's notice have done much better than four points against Chelsea, Roma and Aston Villa? The November international break has always functioned as a critical point for English clubs. Fail to pull the trigger now when there is time to get your feet under the desk and familiarize yourself with players -- who, for once, will have a few days back at the training ground after their commitments around the globe -- before the festive fixture list bears its teeth. In that context, sacking a relatively inexperienced coach like Carrick probably lessens the relegation risk somewhat.

Recent findings suggest that so, in principle, does hiring Pochettino. Here is a coach with over 400 games at the helm of English clubs, whose first job in the country with Southampton has afforded him some experience of the tight margins needed to avoid the drop zone. It was his work at Tottenham that so enamored Sir Alex Ferguson. Over five and a half years he forged Spurs into contenders for (but not winners of) the biggest prizes in the sport. Aggressive, attacking football with a young side imbued with English talent: everything except the silverware screams Manchester United in their pomp.

In a recent development, the price of that success was Pochettino's identity and Tottenham's intermingling. No bad thing when you are as successful as he was at first but it may have given the Argentine an expectation about his role in club football that he has brushed up against in subsequent jobs. At Chelsea he took umbrage at the hierarchy's insistence on affording him young signings rather than the veterans he wanted. The idea that set pieces should sit somewhat outside his jurisdiction and under "specialists" was not popular. At Tottenham, Pochettino had become accustomed to working cheek to jowl with executive chairman and part-owner Daniel Levy. Chelsea, like most Premier League clubs, have established numerous layers between the man in the dugout and the owners. He may not lose his rag in the manner of Antonio Conte but Pochettino is a deeply political operator. Any man who is not afraid to say what he sees could create a great deal of friction when he sees what has been going on at United these last few years.

When he left Stamford Bridge the sense was that Pochettino was yesterday's man in the rapidly evolving world of the Premier League, even though in retrospect it appears he left strong foundations for Enzo Maresca to build on. That view was clearly not one that senior figures at United entirely discounted. After all, at the time they were seriously considering sacking Erik ten Hag after finishing eighth in the Premier League. Pochettino was among the names they considered before doubling down on the soon-to-be-deposed Dutchman.

Sources indicate that that was not the only time United could have got Pochettino. Indeed, when he left Paris Saint-Germain in the summer of 2022, he was interviewed before Ten Hag got the job. That was the most formal approach but there was also the restaurant summit with Ferguson at a Mayfair restaurant when Louis van Gaal was on the brink. And of course there was the chance to hire the 54-year-old in that window earlier this year when Carrick's interim spell was coming to an end and Pochettino had not yet recommitted to the USMNT.

Going for a coach they have consistently decided is not the best option for them will now cost them $10 million for his compensation plus the cost of his sizeable staff. The evidence of PSG, Chelsea and the USMNT is he can deliver to (realistic) expectations. In all likelihood things stabilize under Pochettino, the specter of relegation cast off. The scenario where he takes them down? It probably reflects yesterday's man taking a job at a club still enamored with an outdated vision of management. Pochettino is probably the most Ferguson-coded manager United have employed since the great man's anointed successor. His intense style of play will need willing participants and even if he finds them, it will also take time. That much was as apparent at the clubs where it clicked -- one win in his first seven league games with Southampton, three in nine at Spurs -- as it was elsewhere. Time is not a commodity a side in 18th place can really trade in.

Though Phil Neville was quite scathing in his assessment of Noussair Mazraoui, Ayden Heaven, Leny Yoro and Diogo Dalot on Sunday -- "that back four gets you relegated" -- in pure talent terms United should be absolutely fine. You can question how many players in the squad make up the core of the title-contending outfit they aspire to be but there has been plenty of decent business done buying decent players from decent Premier League teams. Bryan Mbeumo, Matheus Cunha, (in theory right now if not in practice) Youri Tielemans.

According to recent reports, getting another left back and another forward in January would solve a few complications created by more injury-addled players. Then again so would the players on the roster executing better. United rank fourth in the league for non-penalty xG but 11th for goals. Maybe that is because of their wayward finishing. Opta's shooting goals added metric, which assesses the likelihood of a goal being scored pre- and post-shot, ranks this team 17th in the league on -3.57. You wouldn't expect that to hold all season long, particularly when some of the worst offenders are Bruno Fernandes and Cunha. Of course, if it did, then yes, United would be in real trouble.

The same at the other end. Yoro met a free kick with a fine header at Old Trafford on Sunday, drawing a springy save from a goalkeeper who could not stop the ball being turned in on the rebound. The slight concern is the goalkeeper was Senne Lammens and that was the fourth error leading to a goal that United have made this season. Low-volume statistics like these can occasionally betray you but in this case it speaks to a truth clear for all to see; the United defense is too slap-dashy. Young and old, players at Old Trafford have learned that basic errors rarely lead to lasting consequences. If this clumsiness continues -- and it should not be treated as a given that it does -- then the crisis could deepen.

It has been revealed that it's worth saying from the off that if you're rooting for chaos you'd want to see Manchester United's numbers trend down quite dramatically for there to be much in the analytics that states 18th or worse. The "best" relegated sides of recent years are probably Leicester City in 2022-23, sent down to the Championship on 34 points and -0.39 non-penalty xG difference (npxGD) per game, and West Ham three years later. They slipped through the trap door on 39 points and -0.26 npxGD, just a shade worse than Tottenham. Manchester United have sunk to levels below that in past seasons but not this.

Right now there is a long way to go to catch up with the worst teams in the league so far. Ipswich Town have accrued points and look to be a hard out but they are averaging -0.67 npxG difference per game. They are the worst of the newly promoted sides but both Hull City (-0.5) and Coventry City (-0.48) are delivering worrying analytics. The former have the advantage of those points they accrued early in the season and Hull deserve credit for how sparky and organized they are given the talent deficit Sergej Jakirovic is working with. Apply some of those principles with United's talent and competence is no longer the limit.

It isn't just the promoted sides that look bad. Sunderland have a case of difficult second-season syndrome. The best that can be mentioned for Newcastle is that, like Hull, they've banked some fortuitous points. We can maybe ignore Aston Villa given how rarely their xG reflects the results Unai Emery gets.

Then there is Crystal Palace and, well, yikes. In the six seasons before this one only seven teams have had a worse npxGD per game than Palace's -0.86, which is a true marker of inadequacy. These levels Pierre Sage has plummeted the Conference League winners to aren't much better than Norwich City in 2021-22, Luton Town in 2023-24 or the carnival of ineptitude that was Leicester and Southampton two years ago. Palace are bad. So, so bad.

Industry observers note that at least they are in results terms. The talent doesn't seem that bad even if the drip-drip of departures over the last year -- Oliver Glasner, Maxence Lacroix, Marc Guehi, Eberechi Eze -- has lowered their ceiling. With a Thomas Frank in charge you could see them move back on the right path rapidly. Maybe the northeast triumvirate swing upwards too. Suddenly then there might be a space opening up for a team that is both bad and unlucky. That is, of course, assuming that there are three spots opened up for relegated teams this season.

According to recent reports, of course Manchester City might yet have a spot in next season's Championship with their name on it. City were found to have breached 114 of the Premier League's rules by an independent commission, a verdict they are in the midst of appealing.

In a recent development, separate to the process of establishing whether the commission erred in its duties is the matter of sanctioning City. That will be decided by the same three-person panel though it is not yet clear when the hearing will take place nor what the Premier League will expect. Given the abrasive language used by the league about one of its member clubs, it is hard to see them settling for a proposal that does not end with City out of the top flight at the end of the season.

It has been revealed that the Premier League wants this process wrapped up comprehensively but swiftly. Much of the football world expects City to get hit hard, hence why bookmakers have Enzo Maresca's side among the three most likely teams to be relegated. A sweeping points deduction at the Etihad Stadium would be greeted with delight around Old Trafford for many reasons. The fact that it might insulate United from their own mismanagement is certainly one of them.

According to recent reports, there are, however, no guarantees that this process will reach its conclusion before the end of the season. City could endure, dragging out a process they have made plain they believe to be compromised at its most basic principles. Can they keep the wheels spinning for another seven-plus months? Or argue their way to the sort of punishment that does not send them off the edge of the Premier League map? It may be hard to do but it is the sort of unlikely event that, for the time being, might be required to send United to the Championship.

Sources indicate that laLiga president Javier Tebas has published a dated list of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, Real Madrid's board and Real Madrid TV. The post comes a month after Madrid demanded his resignation and six days before Pérez reports to the club's members.

Sources indicate that javier Tebas has turned Real Madrid’s charge sheet back on the club. In a long thread on X titled ‘Who attacks whom?’, the LaLiga president set out years of attacks on the competition by Florentino Pérez, the club’s board and Real Madrid TV. A newspaper column by journalist Tomás González-Martín prompted the thread. The columnist had argued that LaLiga’s president should not spend his time attacking one of the league’s member clubs.

The list closes with the Real Madrid–Villarreal match. Tebas notes Real Madrid TV called LaLiga “adulterated and corrupt” that day. The channel also spoke of systemic corruption and used the phrase “filthy Negreira league”, in his account.

In a recent development, earlier entries go back more than a year. According to Iusport, the list includes a statement approved by Real Madrid’s board on 3 February 2025. It claimed the system was structurally corrupt and that the competition had been manipulated and adulterated. Tebas also quotes a press conference on 12 May 2026, in which Pérez stated Real Madrid’s enemy is always LaLiga. Another entry is Real Madrid TV director Jesús Alcaide. On 4 August 2025, Alcaide said the league was adulterated from the start. He pointed to the fixture calendar and the refusal to postpone Madrid’s opening game against Osasuna.

According to recent reports, tebas presented the post as part of his remit. His job, he wrote, extends to defending the clubs even when the person questioning them is Real Madrid’s president. He also rejected the idea that Pérez and Real Madrid should always be treated as one and the same. That distinction leaves him room to target the club’s president without casting it as an attack on the club.

According to recent reports, the thread follows Madrid’s official statement of 16 October. The club mentioned Tebas’s repeated conduct made him institutionally unfit for his posts and called him a blight on Spanish football. It wanted him gone from LaLiga and from the federation, the body that includes the Technical Committee of Referees.

The same day, EFE reported that Tebas had compared Real Madrid TV’s methods with propaganda techniques used by Joseph Goebbels, the Nazi propaganda minister. Tebas said the comparison was about technique, not ideology or Madrid fans. A day later, the club’s website ran a round-up of international coverage of the comparison.

Recent findings suggest that the dispute also runs through the courts. A separate appeal ruling upheld a February 2024 first-instance judgment in LaLiga’s favour. Real Madrid said it disagreed strongly and would take the case to the Supreme Court.

The ordinary assembly opens at 9:00 on first call and 10:00 on second call, with Pérez’s report as its opening item.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Izzy Goodwin has scored three goals in five WSL appearances for London City.

London City Lionesses forward Izzy Goodwin has been named in the England squad for the first time for the World Cup qualifying play-off against Ukraine.

The 23-year-old has been in great form this month and scored in front of England manager Sarina Wiegman at Emirates Stadium on Sunday in a 1-1 draw with Arsenal.

"We have always seen her as a huge talent with potential," Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live.

According to recent reports, "I think London City are developing really well in the games they have revealed. She is tall and can head a ball attacking-wise, but also defending.

It has been revealed that "She is really quick with her feet and can score goals. I really want to see her in our environment, what she can bring and how close she is to the level that we expect.".

There is also a first call-up for goalkeeper Katie Cox, on loan at Nottingham Forest from Chelsea, while Manchester United midfielder Ella Toone returns.

Manchester City duo Niamh Charles and Alex Greenwood, who is injured, are among those to miss out.

Recent findings suggest that the Lionesses play Ukraine in Spain on 1 December before hosting them at Wembley on 5 December. The winner qualifies for next year's Women's World Cup.

"We know what's at stake in these games and our focus is on producing two strong performances to secure our place at the World Cup," said Wiegman.

"We have worked hard to put ourselves in this position and now we have to finish the job.

"Ukraine will provide a challenge and we will prepare with the same focus and determination that we always do.".

Chelsea defender Lucy Bronze could make her 150th appearance at Wembley in the second leg.

England travel to Pinatar, Spain a few days before the first leg and opted not to play a friendly match during this extended international break.

"The first part of the block we are [at St George's Park]. We have training sessions and a period of time where we can do some tactical stuff," added Wiegman.

"We also selected more players so that helps us create situations where we can train things and everyone is crucial. I'm really excited to get ready for these games.".

Sarina Wiegman led England to victory at Euro 2022 and Euro 2025.

Wiegman was speaking to media at St George's Park for the first time since signing a fresh contract that will run until the end of Euro 2029.

It means she could oversee England's fortunes at next year's World Cup if they beat Ukraine, as well as heading up a Team GB squad at the 2028 Olympic Games.

Asked why she wanted to extend her stay, Wiegman told BBC Radio 5 Live: "Well, first of all the FA is happy with me and I'm really happy with them.

"I'm really grateful for that environment. That is one [reason]. Secondly, I still feel a great connection with staff and players, and of course the country!

It has been revealed that "Then we have the challenges ahead. The major tournaments always motivate me. You don't get many moments with the team because it's not like it is at a club.

"In a tournament, you have those moments where you are really together, you can get somewhere with the group and that really excites me.

It has been revealed that "Yes, the Olympics would be really great. Next year it's the World Cup, then it's the Olympics, then it's the Euros â that journey ahead really excites me.".

Wiegman's contract renewal was kept under wraps and it came as a surprise following their two-legged victory over Greece in October.

The Dutchwoman, who has guided England to successive European titles, remarked conversations had been ongoing for a while but she had not planned ahead.

"When I signed that first contract in 2020 to join in 2021, it was a four-year contract and I thought, 'ok, this is a long contract, it would be really great if things go well'.

In a recent development, "We all got so excited so I signed another contract until 2027 and now I have until 2029. That is eight years. I never expected that. I also never planned so far ahead.

"I want to feel that I can contribute to the environment and the development of things. I also want that from the other party. You want it to fit and for it to work.

"That decision came over time. At one point you think: 'Yeah, I'm getting really excited again.' That is what you want. To feel the energy, to feel the excitement.

According to recent reports, "I still think we have things we can improve. We know the game is improving so swiftly so we have to adapt all the time. When you stand still, you are lost.".

Wiegman is also determined to improve as a coach and has enjoyed overseeing the development of younger talent as the Lionesses transition.

In a recent development, "It starts with me and about how I am going to develop. I keep learning things about myself too. You need to know yourself really well to do this job," she added.

"The staff and the players will always challenge me in the right ways. It goes back and forth. That is what I want. I really want to improve myself all the time.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Antonio Conte has explained why he originally decided to join Inter and why he decided to leave immediately after winning the Serie A title in 2020-21: ‘We want to break Juventus’s dominance in Italy’.

Conte has made headlines in Italy with his upcoming interview with Cronache di Spogliatoio, which has been teased on social media over the last few days. In a clip released on Wednesday, Conte admitted that he would one day like to return to Juventus to ‘close the cycle’ and named several instances where he had been close to returning to Turin.

Another teaser was released on Thursday, with Conte explaining why he decided to join Inter in 2019 and why he decided to leave the Nerazzurri immediately after winning the Serie A title.

Conte had admitted that he had been available and willing to return to Juventus before moving to Inter, but the Bianconeri went with Maurizio Sarri instead, which was part of the reason why Conte decided to join the Nerazzurri instead.

“There have been moments in the past where [Juventus and I] could have reunited, but it’s been difficult because two things have to align. I have to be available and Juventus have to be looking for a coach who isn’t presently employed.

Sources indicate that “There have been two instances. Once, when Juventus decided to hire Maurizio Sarri, I was available and later ended up at Inter. Then there was a second time when I was free, just as Giuntoli arrived. Giuntoli decided to go for Motta and I went to Napoli.”.

In the latest clip of Conte’s Cronache di Spogliatoio interview, he explained further: “[Beppe] Marotta and [Steven] Zhang came to me and noted ‘we want you to bring us back to winning ways, we haven’t won the league in 10 years, we want to break Juventus’s dominance in Italy and impose ourselves abroad’.

“The goal from the club was clear, so we started on a latest journey together. What you see is what you get with me in every situation. If we are heading in a certain direction and we’ve agreed on it, then that is where we must go.”.

Conte feels that he was let down by the Inter management and claims that he left after learning that his title-winning squad could have immediately been dismantled.

Leading goalscorer Romelu Lukaku and star wing-back Achraf Hakimi were sold during the following transfer window.

“I left Inter because we had just won the Scudetto and we had a meeting where I was told that practically any player could be sold in the summer.

“The agreement was different to what it was before: Let’s build ourselves up and tear down Juventus’s dominance and then create a strong and long-lasting structure that will make us competitive in Europe.”.

The full interview with Conte is set to be released on Friday.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

By BOBBY MANZI, FOOTBALL REPORTER.

Published: 08:16 EST, 19 November 2026 | Updated: 09:08 EST, 19 November 2026.

Premier League clubs have voted to protect the organisation's bigwigs from any individual legal action taken by Manchester City's sponsors.

Instead, the clubs - including City themselves - will foot any legal bills incurred by a potential corporate defamation suit.

Daily Mail Sport understands there was widespread support from clubs to insulate Premier League chief executive Richard Masters and the four other league directors.

Nottingham Forest and City are believed to have opposed the motion.

The matter was the first item on the agenda at the Premier League shareholders' meeting in the Savoy Hotel on Thursday and was addressed quickly with limited discussion.

Clubs had a paper for the proposed rule change before the meeting and there was significant support to extend the legal protection to individuals on the league's board.

This marks the first time since the Premier League’s inception that insurance arrangements for its board members have been reviewed.

Premier League clubs will foot the bill if Manchester City's sponsors sue for defamation.

In September, City were found guilty of serious breaches of the Premier League's financial rules after a seven-year legal process.

An independent commission appointed by the Premier League found City inflated their revenues by £900million – disguising money from their Abu Dhabi ownership group as sponsorship revenue.

Etihad Airways, owned by the Abu Dhabi government, denied being ‘involved in improper commercial arrangements’ and mentioned it was considering legal action in response to the verdict.

Meanwhile, another City sponsor, Etisalat - a telecommunications firm - is also weighing up legal action.

City, though, maintain their innocence and are appealing the decision, which could see them relegated from the top flight.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Aston Villa goalkeeper Zion Suzuki went from being serenaded with a chorus of “world’s No 1” to making a bizarre blunder that denied Unai Emery’s side a third successive Premier League victory.

The Villa manager, however, preferred to focus on a string of crucial saves from Suzuki rather than the uncharacteristic mistake that allowed Fulham to collect a deserved point.

It all went wrong for the hosts just after the hour mark in a match where Fulham provided more than a few scares before finding the net in unexpected fashion.

Alex Iwobi, who had been denied superbly by a Suzuki save just moments earlier, swung in a corner. It was right on top of the Villa goalkeeper, who tried to keep it out but only succeeded in fumbling it over the line. A frantic attempt to gather the ball was in vain and goal-line technology confirmed the goal stood.

Zion Suzuki drops Alex Iwobi's corner and Fulham are level! 🫨 https://t.co/KwLFMRpKqk.

Suzuki appeared to have been put off by the presence of Fulham’s Shea Charles, but Emery refused to single out the player for criticism.

“I prefer to speak about the saves that he made,” the Villa manager noted. “This is part of football. I think he played fantastically and he is doing a lot of saves so he can make one mistake. It is part of football. We can be mature about this.

It has been revealed that “I still want to see consistency. Over the last five Premier League matches, we are winning three and drawing two. It’s not bad but with our poor start it’s not enough.

Industry observers note that “We have to change our mind quickly for Tuesday against Barcelona. We want to test ourselves at this level.”.

Villa go to the Nou Camp with a 100 per cent Champions League record to their name this season. But they will need to improve on Saturday evening’s performance to get a result in Spain.

As well as Suzuki’s error, a 14th-minute penalty miss from John McGinn also proved costly.

Recent findings suggest that it was awarded after Leon Goretzka, making his full league debut for Villa, saw his header hit Sander Berge’s raised hand. Nobody appealed at the time but referee Sam Barrott was sent to the touchline monitor by VAR to review the incident and gave the spot-kick.

Recent findings suggest that mcGinn’s attempt, however, hit the crossbar and the chance to take an early lead went begging. The Villa captain seemed a strange choice to take the spot-kick as he has only ever scored one career penalty, but Emery defended the choice, saying: “We analysed the penalty takers in the squad and it was McGinn here.”.

In a recent development, penalty MISSED! John McGinn hits the bar 💥 https://t.co/2kBYkYA2BY.

Sources indicate that nicolas Jackson was on hand to ease Villa’s nerves before the break, though. the Villa manager had said before the game that the striker’s goalscoring capability meant he was capable of matching the likes of Harry Kane. His assessment was backed up by Jackson scoring the opening goal, after 40 minutes, which summed up the striker in one moment of pure power combined with agility.

Collecting Johan Manzambi’s superbly weighted pass, Jackson forced his way past two defenders before sliding in the goal that put Villa ahead.

Emery’s touchline celebrations remarked it all as the Senegal forward continues to flourish under the man who knew how to get the best out of him at Villarreal.

Nicolas Jackson scores his fifth league goal in five games! 🔥 https://t.co/W0xmFtW1Gt.

Suzuki has also flourished under Emery and he kept Villa in the game with some superb saves.

It has been revealed that when Antonee Robinson crossed for Gonzalo Garcia, his step over allowed Oscar Bobb in for what looked like his second goal in successive games. But Suzuki pulled off a stunning fingertip save. That had Villa supporters singing: “Zion Suzuki, the world’s No 1”.

Industry observers note that robinson put in another cross and Suzuki got a touch that was enough to make Garcia put his shot wide. Villa were living dangerously and the Japanese goalkeeper made another outstanding stop to keep out Iwobi’s header. But then it all went wrong for Suzuki when he fumbled Iwobi’s corner.

That allowed Fulham’s recent revival under manager, Alvaro Arbeloa, to continue – they now have seven points from their past three games.

Industry observers note that “We spoke at half-time about what we had to do,” Arbeloa said. “If you want to win a game you have to fight and I think we have to believe in our way, we’ve shown we can beat anyone in the way that we play but we have to be aggressive.

“We created so many chances and at the end it’s one point in a difficult stadium. I’m so happy with the second half because of the way we played, this is the team that we want to be.”.

They have good players and they can make chances. We were unlucky with the goal but we tried to keep fighting. It is important not to lose these games.”.

On Zion Suzuki’s mistake for Fulham’s equaliser:.

In a recent development, “It is frustrating because we do not want to concede goals but it can happen to everyone. Zion is a great guy, great goalkeeper. He will learn from it. We will support him and go again.”.

Industry observers note that tonight sees a battle between two Spaniards at Villa Park as Aston Villa host Fulham. Both sides are looking to bounce back from disappointing midweeks having been knocked out of the League Cup; Aston Villa lost 3-0 at Bournemouth, while Fulham fell to a 1-0 defeat at home against Crystal Palace.

After a slow start to the season in the league, Aston Villa’s form has picked up, which includes handing Manchester City their first defeat of the season a week ago. After this evening, Aston Villa have games against Barcelona and Manchester United before the international break but Unai Emery has insisted his full focus is on this game.

According to recent reports, “If we are thinking after the match against Fulham, then we are making a mistake and we are completely wrong,” Emery noted. “We are prioritising the Premier League, and this is the message. To keep our consistency and demands means that each match is a test.”.

Having failed to win any of their first six league games, Fulham have now won back-to-back Premier League games, with consecutive 1-0 wins over Hull and Coventry, which has lifted them out of the relegation zone.

“It [managing in England] is a very tough challenge but I am so happy to be here,” Alvaro Arbeloa said. “I am where I want to be and I am really enjoying my days. I want to win games and I think we are performing well but we need to improve.

“They [Aston Villa] are very compact, they defend so well and even with the ball they know what they have to do. And they have top players, and when you have a top coach with top players, normally you have a top team. I think right now he [Unai Emery] is one of the best coaches in the world. He is very, very good, he improves everything every year. It does not matter where he is coaching, he is doing an amazing job, and for me also it is a very good challenge to face him.”.

According to recent reports, in the two league meetings between these sides last season, it was one win apiece; Aston Villa won this fixture 3-1 just over a year ago before Fulham won 1-0 at Craven Cottage back in April. Team news from Villa Park to follow shortly.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that A court in Asturias has convicted the Real Oviedo supporter who made monkey gestures at Kylian Mbappé of a hate crime. The case adds to a growing list of criminal convictions for racist abuse of Real Madrid players in Spanish grounds.

Sources indicate that the Real Oviedo supporter who racially abused Kylian Mbappé at the Carlos Tartiere has been convicted of a hate crime. The Second Section of the Audiencia Provincial de Asturias delivered the verdict on 17 November 2026. It was a verdict by agreement, known in Spain as conformidad.

The abuse came during Real Oviedo v Real Madrid on 24 August 2025. The fan made monkey gestures and noises in the 37th minute. Real Madrid’s players were celebrating Mbappé’s opening goal at the time.

It has been revealed that the man will not go to prison as long as he keeps to the terms of his sentence. The term is suspended on condition that he stays away from football stadiums hosting official competitions for two years, Real Madrid said in an official statement. The prosecuting parties also tied the suspension to a ban from LaLiga stadiums and a ban on approaching Mbappé. The defendant accepted these conditions.

The fine was set at six months at a daily rate of €8. He is also barred from working in education, teaching, sport or leisure for three years and 11 months.

The case was charged under article 510.2.a of the Spanish Criminal Code. LaLiga filed the original complaint. It also supplied expert lip-reading evidence that proved key to resolving the case. Real Madrid later joined the proceedings as a private prosecutor.

Industry observers note that the ruling is LaLiga’s twelfth conviction for racism in Spanish football, Servimedia reported. The league presented the outcome as proof of its commitment to fighting racism.

The Carlos Tartiere has featured in this list before. In April 2026, a supporter was convicted over abuse of Marcus Rashford at Real Oviedo v FC Barcelona. That person received a nine-month prison sentence. Another conviction, handed down in September 2025, followed abuse of Iñaki Williams at an Espanyol v Athletic Club match from the 2019/20 season.

Industry observers note that for Real Madrid, the verdict extends a run of cases involving its own players. The club has listed earlier convictions for racist abuse at Mestalla, Son Moix, Vallecas and the José Zorrilla. The Valladolid case ended on 21 May 2025. The Audiencia Provincial de Valladolid convicted five people of hate crimes for abusing Vinícius Júnior at the José Zorrilla on 30 December 2022. Each received a one-year prison sentence.

The pattern points to clubs and the league pursuing racist abuse through the criminal courts rather than leaving it to stadium sanctions alone. In the Oviedo case, the combination of a league complaint and lip-reading evidence was decisive.

Real Madrid is now acting as private prosecutor in other cases involving similar incidents against its players.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

As Nvidia, one of the world's most valuable companies, grapples with CEO Jensen Huang's romantic relationship with an alleged Chinese spy, attention is turning to the much smaller company she worked for.

Alice H., the alleged spy, worked as an executive for Megaspeed, a Singapore-based data center and AI computing organization. It manages data center access, including for some major Chinese tech firms such as Alibaba.

Recent findings suggest that according to Megaspeed's website as of November 2026, the firm advertises itself as an "Nvidia cloud partner", saying it provides "computing power product services covering Nvidia's entire GPU product line." GPU stands for Graphic Processing Unit, a specialized electronic circuit that are in high demand for artificial intelligence (AI) applications, because they are designed to handle high numbers of parallel mathematical calculations. Megaspeed claims it provides access for clients to Nvidia's advanced GB200 NVL72 ​computing system.

Industry observers note that this type of firm is often referred to as a "neocloud". It buys Nvidia chips and computing power and then rents it out — in this case, at multiple sites across south-east Asia, to different companies. The US has set up strict export controls to prevent that Nvidia's high-performance chips end up in China, because it sees China as a competitor in the global AI race. It also does not want data centers made up of Nvidia chips to be owned by Chinese companies. It does, however, tolerate that data center compute with Nvidia chips be rented out to Chinese companies like Alibaba, and occasionally allows the export of Nvidia chips for specific purposes.

Megaspeed has bought billions of dollars worth of Nvidia's products in recent years and has been accused of breaching US export controls to divert Nvidia chips into China.

In December 2025, Bloomberg reported that the "once-obscure" Megaspeed had become the biggest buyer of Nvidia's chips in all of south-east Asia and that the US government was investigating its ownership structure and whether or not it was smuggling Nvidia chips into China.

According to recent reports, at the same time, Singapore police began an investigation into whether or not Megaspeed had "violated local laws" without specifying which ones. Those investigations are believed to be still ongoing.

On December 23, 2025, Megaspeed strenuously denied any wrongdoing in a statement — which still appears as the first page for visitors to the firm's website as of November 2026.

"There has been no evidence of any violations concerning the illicit transfer of chips or any illegal activities, and this demonstrates that we are a compliant and legitimate company," it mentioned. "We operate fully within the bounds of all applicable export control regulations and maintain the highest standards of legal and ethical conduct.".

The US government investigation began in 2024. The Commerce Department initially began looking into Megaspeed, but the US Justice Department has since taken over. According to the Fresh York Times, this switch came about after an Nvidia executive directly contacted the Commerce Department about the investigation.

Megaspeed was founded in 2015 and was originally called 7Road International. It changed its name to Megaspeed in March 2023. It is owned by the Singapore-registered Swiftdata, which was set up in October 2023.

Its rise in prominence coincided with a sharp increase in assets, which increased from $33 million in 2023 to $3 billion in 2024.

Sources indicate that alice H., the woman accused of being a Chinese spy, had an affair with Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang. She is widely seen as an influential figurehead at Megaspeed. She also served as the firm's managing director of Megaspeed for eight months in 2023.

The Financial Times reported on Monday that Alice H. leveraged her close access to Jensen Huang and Nvidia to pitch AI chips deals to Chinese investors.

To view this video please enable JavaScript, and consider upgrading to a web browser that supports HTML5 video.

Industry observers note that the newspaper said that in early 2025, Alice H. sought investment in China for a data center project in south-east Asia, and cited their easy access to Nvidia chips and close relationship with Alibaba.

Sources indicate that alibaba lent money to Megaspeed in June 2024, via subsidiaries. It has remained Megaspeed's largest client, according to reporting by the Financial Times.

According to recent reports, in December 2025, Nvidia said its own inquiry into Megaspeed had found no evidence of chips being diverted and that the manufacturer was fully owned and operated outside of China, with no Chinese shareholders. The company told Bloomberg at the time that it had visited Megaspeed's facilities on multiple occasions and had seen nothing untoward.

Megaspeed is one of several companies accused of smuggling Nvidia's chips into China or finding ways to give Chinese companies access to them.

Nvidia's high-performance chips are seen as essential for companies looking for the most advanced form of supercomputing to use and develop various AI applications.

Back in 2022, the Biden Administration began severely restricting the sale of the US's most advanced chips to China, part of the two countries' growing rivalry to achieve AI dominance.

However, an illegal smuggling and underground network was soon set up, with many vendors operating to get the chips into China and selling them on to companies there.

In December 2025, US authorities shut down the operations of Hao Global, a US-based shell organization with links to China which plead guilty to smuggling Nvidia chips to China.

In June 2026, Taiwanese government agencies raided the offices of Super Micro Computer as part of an investigation into the smuggling of Nvidia chips to China.

While export restrictions have been eased significantly under the Trump administration, there are still significant blocks and restrictions on the most advanced Nvidia chips.

In December 2025, the Trump administration approved several Chinese companies to buy or handle advanced Nvidia H200 chips, a move that sparked significant concern among the US security establishment.

However, that deal has not led to a significant flow of Nvidia chips moving legally to China, amid strict US licencing controls and official reluctance from Beijing to publicly promote Nvidia chips to the detriment of its own alternatives.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Jess Carter made 83 appearances across all competitions for Gotham FC.

England defender Jess Carter has completed a move to Bay FC after leaving Gotham FC as a free agent.

The 29-year-old has signed a contract that will keep her with Bay FC - a club based in the San Francisco Bay Area - until 2028, with the option for an additional year.

Carter joined Latest York-side Gotham in July 2024 after a six-year spell with Chelsea that saw her win the Women's Super League on five occasions.

"Coming to Bay FC is a fresh challenge, and that's something I'm excited about," said Carter.

In a recent development, "I've been fortunate to be part of some successful teams, and I know how much work goes into winning. I'm looking forward to getting to know this group, earning the trust of my team-mates and doing my part to help us move forward.".

Carter played in all 30 of Gotham's matches in 2026 as the club won the NWSL Shield - given to the league's regular-season champions.

She also helped Gotham win the NWSL Championship in 2025, when they defeated Washington Spirit in the final.

"Jess has been a big part of what we've accomplished as a club, and we're very thankful for the contributions she's made during her time here," mentioned Yael Averbuch West, the president of football operations for Gotham.

Carter, who has 56 senior England caps, was part of the squad that won the 2022 European Championships, while she appeared in all six games as the Lionesses defended their title last summer.

"Jess has consistently demonstrated her quality in championship-winning environments at both club and international level," remarked Bay FC's chief football officer Paul Green, who worked with Carter at Chelsea.

"I've seen her development and the professionalism she brings every day. She will bring valuable experience to Bay FC, and we're delighted to welcome her to the club.".

The 2027 NWSL regular season kicks off in February.

Former England and Chelsea star Joe Cole has highlighted the vital importance of protecting grassroots pitches across the capital, warning "you can’t produce any footballers without football pitches.".

The 45-year-old enjoyed an illustrious playing career, which included three Premier League titles at Stamford Bridge and 56 caps for the Three Lions, and London’s local playing fields played a pivotal role in shaping his journey to the top.

Industry observers note that established in 1890, the charity works to safeguard the capital’s green spaces, inspiring future generations to follow in the footsteps of sporting greats. Speaking exclusively to FourFourTwo, Cole admitted the nomination means a great deal to him.

"London and football are two of the things most dearest to my heart," Cole remarked. "I’m a London kid. I was born in Camden Town, and obviously football is my passion, so the two things together make perfect sense, and they do a great job there.

"We need to protect the green space, not just for football, but for every sport, for kids to play, particularly in London. We have a rich history of producing footballers. You can’t produce any footballers without football pitches – whether that be five-a-side, seven-a-side, 11-a-side, cricket pitches, anything for young people to go out and be active. It’s about keeping them off the developers and making sure there’s room for kids to play.".

Renowned throughout his career for his street-footballer flair and close control, Cole honed his trademark skills growing up in north London during the 1980s, making the most of whatever space was available.

It has been revealed that "I lived in a ground-floor flat with a tiny garden, so London was my back garden," Cole recalled. "There were no boundaries. There was a bit of grass right outside my house, a wall, and over the back end there was a little concrete seven-a-side pitch.

The statement is enough to make any Scotland fan uncomfortable, but that's been the relaxed theme going into this Nations League campaign among some outside of Hampden.

Euro 2028 has various different access routes, especially for the host nations of England, Republic of Ireland, Scotland and Wales, who even have two spare spaces between them secured before a ball is kicked.

But, in the bleak, barren and grim aftermath of Scotland's 4-0 scudding by Switzerland in St Gallen, "almost impossible" almost feels like a challenge.

According to recent reports, scotland began with three shots at reaching the finals, where they would play at Hampden Park if they made it. We're now down to two.

Sources indicate that they could have qualified for the Euro 2028 finals with help from the Nations League. Not straightforward, but absolutely achievable.

Finish top of group B1 containing Switzerland, Slovenia and North Macedonia, then prevail in the play-off.

In Sebastien Pocognoli's first six games in charge, he failed to deliver that, his latest-look squad and system only offering seven points.

Not only that but that third-place finish has further repercussions.

Sources indicate that scotland's next route lies in the Euro qualifiers, with the draw taking place in Belfast on 6 December. Can't wait.

Pocognoli's team will go into pot three for that, making a shot at progression that much more difficult.

That means the Scots could be drawn in a group with the likes of Serbia, Turkey, Czech Republic, Switzerland, or Austria as their pot 2 opponent.

Sources indicate that for example, Scotland could be in a group with Spain, Switzerland, Kazakhstan and Azerbaijan. Please, no.

The top 12 group winners and the eight best runners-up go straight through, with the rest of the runners-up going into a play-off with the best Nations League non-qualified group winners.

If Scotland make a hash of that, then do not fear...

Uefa is reserving two spots for the two best-ranked host nations who have not qualified after the completion of the qualifying group stage.

It's now feasible this may come into play.

Going on the assumption England - who have just turned over world champions Spain - will qualify, that leaves Scotland, Wales and Ireland. Despite the qualifying draw being in Belfast, Northern Ireland aren't a host nation.

If one of them qualifies through other means, then happy days.

If they do not, then the Scots will need to hope they are not the lowest-ranked team among the three or they face being locked out of their own house party.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club.
  • Industry observers note that spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation.
  • The decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Spain's Supreme Court has refused LaLiga's appeal, making final the annulment of the August 2021 assembly vote on the CVC deal, a case won by Real Madrid and Athletic Club. It is a legal win for the two clubs, but the later December 2021 approval behind LALIGA Impulso remains in force.

Industry observers note that spain’s Supreme Court has thrown out LaLiga’s cassation appeal against the Madrid Provincial Court judgment on the CVC operation. The General Assembly resolution of 12 August 2021, which approved the deal, therefore stays void for good. Real Madrid and Athletic Club brought the winning case. LaLiga now carries the costs of the failed appeal.

The decision closes a five-year legal fight over that single vote. In August 2021, Barcelona, Athletic Club and Real Madrid jointly revealed a challenge to the resolution. They argued it broke Royal Decree-Law 5/2015 and was passed through a highly irregular process.

It has been revealed that real Madrid described the annulled resolution as one of huge economic significance. In the club’s account, it was passed before clubs had enough information to judge the scope, impact and consequences of changes to the operation. The club also highlighted the court’s remark that LaLiga’s appeal tried to replace the Provincial Court’s view with LaLiga’s own self-interested view.

LaLiga reads the decision more narrowly. The annulled assembly approved the term sheet of the CVC project, and the appeal fell for lack of cassation interest. LaLiga stated the court issued a procedural order rather than a judgment endorsing the Provincial Court’s reasoning, and did not examine the substance of the case.

The deal itself does not depend on the annulled vote. LaLiga’s General Assembly approved the LALIGA Impulso project later, on 10 December 2021. Under the deal, clubs received around €2bn in exchange for a share of the value of the competition’s audiovisual rights over 50 years. A new company set up by LaLiga and the fund manages that arrangement. Real Madrid, Barcelona and Athletic Club rejected it and stayed out.

Those December resolutions have survived their own court test. In June 2026, Section 18 of the Madrid Provincial Court rejected in full the appeal by Athletic Club and Real Madrid against them. It upheld the first-instance judgment of 19 February 2024 and ordered both clubs to pay the costs of that hearing. The court found that clubs still own their audiovisual rights, while LaLiga sells them collectively under the law. It also ruled that creating LaLiga Group International, owned jointly by LaLiga and CVC, did not breach the Sports Law or LaLiga’s statutes.

That leaves the practical picture largely unchanged. Iusport, a Spanish sports-law outlet, described the Supreme Court order as having no practical effect on the LaLiga–CVC deal. The ruling still matters for how LaLiga is run, because it confirms that one of its assembly votes on the operation was unlawful. The league insists it respects court decisions and will keep defending the agreements backed by most of its clubs.

The fight over the December agreements is not over either. Real Madrid has taken that ruling to the Supreme Court, which has not yet decided whether to admit the appeal.

General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Nature ↗ Open Full Page

Rethinking corporate climate targets for real-world transitions

📅 19 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 8 min read (1676 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Nature

⏱️ ~8 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • According to recent reports, corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation.
  • This is a preview of subscription content, access via your institution.
  • Access Nature and 54 other Nature Portfolio journals.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, corporate greenhouse gas reduction targets are central to climate action, but they often fall short of driving meaningful business transformation. Despite progress in standardization, current target-setting approaches remain weakened by methodological problems, including inaccurate emissions accounting, excluded emissions sources and limited comparability across companies. More importantly, many corporate targets are disconnected from the real-world sectoral transitions required to meet the Paris Agreement’s temperature goal. Drawing on evidence from four editions of the Corporate Climate Responsibility Monitor and recent literature, we argue that target-setting frameworks should place greater emphasis on systemic changes in business models, technologies and value chains. We propose transition targets as a practical complement to traditional greenhouse gas reduction targets. These targets would incentivize, guide and measure progress towards sector-specific milestones, such as electrification, low-carbon material uptake and the phase-out of emissions-intensive technologies. Embedding transition targets in accountability standards, and eventually in regulation, could help close the gap between corporate climate commitments and real-world action. It would also align corporate target-setting with the physical transition benchmarks introduced by the Paris Agreement’s Global Stocktake. The scientific community has a key role in developing robust, actionable frameworks for corporate decarbonization.

Manchester United have decided to make a managerial change during the November international break and sacked Michael Carrick after a challenging start to the season. The Red Devils have reportedly decided to hire Mauricio Pochettino, who led the United States men's national team at the 2026 World Cup and just signed a fresh deal with the American federation. However, Pochettino had a $10 million release clause in his contract and spoke multiple times about his desire to go back to the English Premier League, after coaching Southampton, Tottenham and Chelsea before making his move to the U.S.

Manchester United have also explored multiple options in the past weeks, and several names emerged as potential candidates for the job. Let's take a look at the top free-agent coaches currently available on the market and identify those who remain open to a move in the near future. For this specific reason we have decided to not include former Manchester City coach Pep Guardiola, who is not looking for a job in the short term.

The Spanish coach left Manchester City ahead of the summer of 2026 and decided to take a break from the world of soccer, despite having a concrete offer in the summer to become the fresh manager of the Italian national team. Guardiola sat down with the Italian federation but then opted to stick to his commitment to take a break. Furthermore, given his close ties to the Manchester City hierarchy and ownership, his name was never going to be considered by the Manchester United board. Here's a list of the top coaches without a job right now:.

In a recent development, the former England national team manager is still searching for his next club after deciding to step down from his international role in order to return to club management. However, he appears unlikely to find a latest position in the short term. This is a challenge presently facing several national team coaches, including former France manager Didier Deschamps. Manchester United had previously shown interest in him, but did not make a concrete approach in recent weeks, despite having the opportunity to do so.

The former Tottenham manager was one of the names that emerged in the past weeks for the Man United job. However, the former Brentford and Spurs manager is now in talks to become the new Crystal Palace manager after a disappointing start to the Premier League season, as the Eagles are at the moment at the bottom of the standings, two points behind Manchester United.

The former Newcastle head coach was one of the names on the list of the Manchester United board of directors in recent weeks. The English head coach left Newcastle in the summer and he's still under contract with the club right now. Any club looking to appoint him would first have to pay a release clause to Newcastle. Despite his Premier League experience, Manchester United did not consider him as a potential replacement. He is now likely to wait until the summer before deciding on his next career move.

An attractive name: the former German national team coach left his job in the summer after the disappointment of the 2026 World Cup, when Germany were kicked out by Paraguay in the round of 32 of the tournament. Nagelsmann, after coaching RB Leipzig and Bayern Munich before moving to the national team, is now likely to move to another league, and the Premier League is definitely a league that can potentially attract him. Let's now see if there will be a job available in the summer, even if the big clubs seem pretty stable at this stage.

Sources indicate that the Italian coach is waiting for the right opportunity to come after the two years spent at Napoli, where he was able to win the Scudetto in his first season in charge, replicating the success he had at Juventus and Inter in his home country. According to reports, Conte would be keen for another Premier League experience after coaching Chelsea and Tottenham but he's not ruling out other clubs. However, Manchester United never made contact with his camp as they didn't want to hire the Italian manager to replace Carrick. Conte has often been regarded as a short-term appointment, having never spent more than three years at any single club throughout his managerial career.

Neuer injury gives Urbig chance to shape Bayern and Germany future

📅 10 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 3 min read (546 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~3 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • It's no secret that getting playing time is crucial to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country .
  • It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception.
  • But when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

It's no secret that getting playing time is crucial to the development of any professional footballer – especially if your aspiration is to become the first-choice goalkeeper for your country . For most national team coaches, only a keeper who is playing regularly for his club merits consideration.

It has been revealed that unsurprisingly, Germany coach Jürgen Klopp is no exception. While he did give Urbig – the backup keeper at Bayern – two starts in his first international break as national team boss, for the upcoming UEFA Nations League matches against Serbia and the Netherlands, Marc-André ter Stegen remains the undisputed No. 1.

But when Klopp gave ter Stegen the nod, Urbig was still spending most of his time on the bench in Munich. But this is set to change after Bayern's recent Bundesliga win over Mainz. The 40-year-old Manuel Neuer asked to be subbed off just before halftime, complaining of severe pain in his right foot.

An examination revealed that Neuer has sustained a partial tendon tear in the foot.

"An injury never comes at the right time, but it's part of the game," Neuer wrote on Instagram.

Recent findings suggest that "I've been through this before, and I'll get through this one too. From now on: full focus on recovery. Until then, I will support the boys on the pitch wherever I can.".

A partial tendon tear usually results in a layoff of six to 12 weeks, depending on the severity of the injury. Given that Neuer's foot already has some pre-existing damage from previous injuries, his recovery could take even longer.

Although Urbig is now the de-facto first-choice keeper for Bayern, he will still have to bide his time in the national team as understudy to ter Stegen. However, there is a general consensus that someday, Urbig will also become Germany's No. 1. With Neuer's contract running out in the summer, the chance to truly make the Bayern goal his own appears likely in the not-too-distant future.

The match on Saturday was Neuer's 550th in the Bundesliga and he also became the oldest player in a league match in Bayern's history when he took the pitch aged 40 years and 225 days. In other words, he can't go on forever.

One of his most famous predecessors in the Bayern goal has already called on him to draw a line under his highly successful career.

"I would tell him: 'Call it a day, Manu!' You have given an incredible amount to football, you have won everything, and you don't have to prove anything to anyone anymore," Sepp Maier, a member of West Germany's 1974 World Cup winning team told Sport1.

According to recent reports, at some point, the now 82-year-old Maier noted, there comes a moment "when your body no longer behaves the way you want it to. And even a Manuel Neuer cannot stave off that moment.".

In a recent development, for now, with ter Stegen playing regularly and performing well for Ajax, Germany coach Klopp is under no pressure to make a change. However, the 34-year-old former Barcelona keeper has, like Neuer, become quite injury-prone in recent years. Whenever he's needed, Urbig will be more than happy to seize his opportunity.

  • On a thrilling Sunday night in Madrid, as 10-man England stunned reigning world champions Spain 3-2 to snap La Roja’s 43-match unbeaten run, Leeds United’s James Trafford and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall announced themselves as the next generation of Three Lions stalwarts.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

According to recent reports, succession planning is one of international football’s trickiest arts, especially when replacing a goalkeeper who has laid claim to the No. 1 shirt for nearly a decade, or trying to fix a left-back spot that has become something of a revolving door.

For Thomas Tuchel, though, the answers to two of England’s biggest long-term headaches have been forged at Elland Road and St James’ Park.

On a thrilling Sunday night in Madrid, as 10-man England stunned reigning world champions Spain 3-2 to snap La Roja’s 43-match unbeaten run, Leeds United’s James Trafford and Newcastle’s Lewis Hall announced themselves as the next generation of Three Lions stalwarts.

Recent findings suggest that for almost 10 years, Jordan Pickford’s status as England’s undisputed No. 1 has been largely uninterrupted, stretching from the 2018 World Cup to last summer’s semi-final run in North America. It left little room for an understudy to build experience or a case for selection.

Sources indicate that moving on from a 94-cap mainstay is never straightforward, which is why Trafford’s decision to swap Manchester City’s bench for regular Premier League football at Leeds in August has proven so vital for Tuchel. Playing week-in, week-out has helped the 24-year-old develop into a ready-made alternative capable of taking the gloves whenever Pickford eventually hangs his up.

Handed a rare start at the Metropolitano and given the chance to test his temperament and major-game mentality against elite opposition, Trafford watched as goals from Harry Kane, Ezri Konsa and Ben White fired England into a 3-0 lead.

It has been revealed that but when Elliot Anderson saw red in the 62nd minute, Leeds’ No.1 was faced with a relentless Spanish siege. Spain racked up 23 shots, seven on target and 2.73 Expected Goals (xG), yet Trafford refused to buckle.

The best features, fun and footballing quizzes, straight to your inbox every week.

The Leeds stopper made five crucial saves - repelling Fermin Lopez from close range, recovering well to deny Lamine Yamal and Marc Cucurella, and producing an outstanding stoppage-time double save to thwart Yamal and Aymeric Laporte - all the while impressing Tuchel with his composure during build-up.

According to recent reports, at left-back, Tuchel’s gratitude to Newcastle should be equally clear. Since Euro 2024, England have cycled through 10 different players in the role, experimenting with the likes of Nico O’Reilly and Myles Lewis-Skelly, right-footed deputies such as Djed Spence, and stopgaps. This is largely because nobody had convincingly locked down the position consistently at club level.

Many felt Hall was unfairly overlooked when Tuchel left him out of the 2026 World Cup squad, a tournament in which England’s left flank seemed to lack balance. But the 22-year-old’s emergence as an indispensable starter for Newcastle, particularly this season, has finally given Tuchel a specialist he can rely on.

It has been revealed that against one of the most dangerous wingers on the planet, Lamine Yamal, Hall was excellent. Defensively, he registered five clearances and two vital first-half interventions inside his own box to snuff out Yamal and Mikel Merino, before drawing two late fouls to relieve pressure in the dying seconds.

In possession, he was just as accomplished, completing five dribbles in the first half alone - more than Spain’s entire 10 outfield players combined. He found a teammate with 30 of his 34 passes (88 per cent accuracy), providing natural left-footed width that facilitated Anthony Gordon's strong performance, too.

According to recent reports, pickford’s experience ensures he won't be surrendering his place without a fight, and Tuchel insisted afterwards that no permanent changing of the guard has taken place. International bosses are ultimately reliant on club environments to forge their stars, so by entrusting Trafford and Hall with pivotal Premier League roles, Leeds and Newcastle are doing the heavy lifting for future tournaments.

Joe joined FourFourTwo as senior digital writer in July 2025 after five years covering Leeds United in the Championship and Premier League. Joe's 'Mastermind' specialist subject is 2000s-era Newcastle United having had a season ticket at St. James' Park for 10 years before relocating to Leeds and later London. Joe takes a keen interest in youth football, covering PL2, U21 Euros, as well as U20 and U17 World Cups in the past, in addition to hosting the industry-leading football recruitment-focused SCOUTED podcast. He is also one of the lucky few to have 'hit top bins' as a contestant on Soccer AM. It wasn't a shin-roller.

Paul McStay is a regular guest at Celtic Park.

Celtic legend Paul McStay notes having a supporters representative on the board would be a significant step to halting the unrest between the club and the fans.

Issues have arisen around a perceived lack of investment in the Scottish Premiership outfit and underachievement in Europe, with one prominent supporters group recently boycotting matches in protest.

Former Scotland international McStay played his entire club career at Celtic, making more than 500 league appearances between 1981 and 1997 and winning three league titles, four Scottish Cups and a League Cup.

Now he is involved with a collection of season-ticket holders, whose aim is to have more say in how the club is run.

The former captain has made his opinion known to members of the board and believes "healthy debate" can resolve the "disconnect".

Why Celtic's next three games could set AGM tone.

Industry observers note that "I think there's issues that have to be resolved just now," McStay said. "When Celtic players, management, directors and supporters are all as one, we will be successful or have a great chance of being successful so my hope is that happens again.

Sources indicate that "To me, it's healthy debate that's required and come up with a solution that helps our drive forward - domestically maintain the success and in Europe. I think that's what the fans want.".

In just under a fortnight, Celtic shareholders will gather at the ground for the club's annual general meeting.

It has been revealed that given the chaos of last year's event, there will be extra eyes and ears on the 2026 AGM on 1 December. And McStay wants change to try and avert more problems.

"The idea is to get enough equity in the club to allow the supporters to have a representative on the board and to me that's important.

Industry observers note that "I know the directors and they just want the best for Celtic. We are allowed opinions and I voice my opinions to them, slightly different from what they're thinking.

Industry observers note that "To have regular Champions League football is what Celtic supporters are hoping for and I think we can achieve that. But just now I think there's a few things that need to be talked about, debated and hopefully we can move forward as a club.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Tenerife won 5-2 at Badajoz in the Copa del Rey despite finishing the match with ten men. The victory keeps their cup run alive ahead of the second-round draw.

Industry observers note that at the Estadio Nuevo Vivero on Wednesday 18 November, Álvaro Cervera’s side booked a place in the second round of the Copa del Rey. The tie had been postponed twice, first after the train accident in Toledo province and then after the death of Tenerife forward Jesús de Miguel on 3 November, who was remembered with a minute’s silence.

In a recent development, cervera started a line-up made up largely of reserves. It still produced a scoreline Tenerife had never recorded in 260 Copa del Rey matches, according to elDiario.es (Canarias Ahora). About 3,000 spectators watched, around 20 per cent of the stadium’s capacity.

Industry observers note that grant-Leon Ranos opened the scoring in the sixth minute from a Marc Mateu assist. Juanjo Sánchez added a second a minute later. Ranos struck again in the 38th minute, set up by Gerard Valentín.

Carlos Beitia pulled one back for Badajoz in the 49th minute. Roko Jureškin was then sent off in the 58th minute. Ten-man Tenerife still extended the lead through substitute Iván Chapela in the 69th minute, assisted by Martin Pečar.

Industry observers note that jorge Barba replied for the hosts in the 74th minute from a Manuel Hernández assist. Víctor Moreno completed the scoring deep into stoppage time, with Álvarez providing the pass.

The Segunda Federación side went into the tie third in their group. They were also unbeaten in seven league matches in a row.

According to recent reports, tenerife have now come through their opening Copa del Rey tie in eight seasons in a row. The win followed a 2-0 victory over AD Ceuta FC. Before that came a run of draws against FC Andorra, Sabadell, Celta de Vigo II and Girona.

Recent findings suggest that this was the first meeting between the clubs in the cup. They had played each other 22 times in Segunda División. Tenerife won ten of those games, Badajoz eight, and four ended level. Tenerife’s previous visit to Badajoz, on 30 March 2003, ended in a 2-1 defeat under David Amaral.

#36795. Inside Gotham FC's move to Icahn Stadium: Debates over pitch quality, fines and the NWSL's logistical struggle
